title: Angular applications
description: For an Angular application: supported versions, sanitization, XSRF, strict templates, subscriptions and bundle budgets.

sources.title: Angular CLI, building applications: size budgets

rules.instruction: Keep the application on an Angular major version in active or long-term support, and upgrade with `ng update`.
rules.verification: Compare the `@angular/core` version in the lockfile with the support table of the Angular releases page.

rules.instruction: Do not call `bypassSecurityTrust*` or write to `innerHTML` through native DOM APIs with untrusted values. Bind through templates or call `DomSanitizer.sanitize`.
rules.verification: Search the change for `bypassSecurityTrust` and direct DOM writes, and record the review of each remaining call with the security owner.

rules.instruction: Keep HttpClient XSRF protection on, and confirm the backend sets the XSRF cookie and checks the header on state-changing requests.
rules.verification: Send a state-changing request without the XSRF header in an integration test and assert that the backend rejects it.
Check `tsconfig.json` for `strictTemplates: false` and run `ng build` on the branch.

rules.instruction: Subscribe in templates with the async pipe, or end manual subscriptions with `takeUntilDestroyed`.
rules.verification: Search the changed components for `subscribe(` without `takeUntilDestroyed`, and test that destroying the component stops the stream.

rules.instruction: Set `maximumWarning` and `maximumError` budgets for the initial bundle in `angular.json`.
rules.verification: Run the production build and compare the reported bundle sizes with the budgets.
